title: Multi-Hop Reasoning Circuits Evade Single-Feature Deception Probes

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Addresses a critical limitation of deception probes: if capable schemers use multi-hop indirect reasoning, single-feature probes will miss them. Directly tests the adequacy of the current probing paradigm for the deception strategies that matter most.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing prompts that require multi-step reasoning to reach a deceptive conclusion where each step looks benign is conceptually very difficult. Ensuring the model actually performs multi-hop deception on a small model is not guaranteed. Dataset construction is the bottleneck.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires careful dataset construction, probes at each layer, comparison between multi-hop and single-step deception. The hardest part (constructing multi-hop deceptive prompts where each step is benign) may take most of the 30 hours with uncertain yield.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
